archetypes.name: gh-cli-contracts
archetypes.rationale: The diff changes gh pr create argv and PR recovery behavior where real CLI compatibility and race handling are load-bearing.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate the gh CLI integration changes around PR creation, current-branch PR lookup, URL parsing, and post-create recovery. Check whether unsupported flags are fully removed while successful create, conflict recovery, transient lag, repo mismatch, and stale branch cases still resolve or fail predictably. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: merge-head-sync
archetypes.rationale: The merge path removes a pre-merge flush and adds PR head OID polling, making race and convergence behavior especially important.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the merge flow for correctness after removing the per-attempt pre-merge run-log flush and adding head OID polling. Focus on whether refreshed PR state is used consistently, retry caps cannot hang, mismatches fail safely, and clean green PRs avoid divergence-triggered CI loops. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: runlog-cleanliness
archetypes.rationale: The new volatile-only run-log skip path performs git cleanup and must not drop substantive artifacts or leave dirty porcelain.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the run-log publish and flush changes that classify refresh sidecars as volatile-only and restore or clean the worktree. Verify the allowlist is narrow, canonical token and timing artifacts still commit on substantive changes, all cleanup failures fail closed, and repo-wide porcelain is checked before push-sensitive paths proceed. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: python311-compat
archetypes.rationale: The runtime floor is lowered to Python 3.11 across code, docs, CI, and lint/type pins, which can drift easily.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check the Python 3.11 compatibility changes across packaging metadata, lint/type configuration, CI matrix, runtime guards, docs, and newly changed Python code. Look for remaining 3.12-only syntax, stale 3.12 probes or documentation, and inconsistencies between runtime requirements and contributor tooling requirements. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: stdout-protocol
archetypes.rationale: The Python ship driver relies on a strict JSON-only stdout contract while adding breadcrumbs and lib-quiet routing.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect the observability changes in the Python driver, CI monitor, and logging utility for stream-contract regressions. Confirm breadcrumbs, warnings, redaction, and quiet-mode routing cannot contaminate stdout when callers expect a single JSON object, and that operational ShipError paths still map to structured stalled results. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: shell-sete-routing
archetypes.rationale: The bootstrap routing parser fix targets subtle set -e behavior in sourced shell helpers with file-first and stdout-fallback passes.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the bootstrap routing parser and its harness for set -e safety when environment keys are already populated before fallback parsing runs. Check preserve-coder behavior, empty-value handling, exported variable consistency, and whether the new test actually reproduces the prior false failure in both intended modes. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
